Operating robots in dynamic environments is becoming increasingly complex with the growing presence of mobile agents. To manage this challenge, we introduce a novel method for automatically creating restricted areas where certain objects cannot be located. By incorporating these restrictions into motion planning, we effectively manage collisions with stationary objects without needing to compute full motion plans. This paper outlines a technique where robot paths are generated to avoid static obstacles at boundary locations only. An example is demonstrated using a state-space expansion method based on a cost function designed to minimize contact frequency. An experiment illustrates the algorithm's operation and its capabilities are assessed against scenarios involving multiple agents and obstacles.

Visual localisation is a fundamental and extensively researched computer vision task that determines a camera's position and orientation relative to a scene. This task gains significant importance in various applications such as autonomous driving and robotics, particularly when dealing with repetitive textures and camera pose inaccuracies. This research proposes a visual relocalisation approach that integrates visual and geometric information to enhance robustness and precision. This method employs point cloud-based, depth-sensitive features combined with pose-robust descriptor learning, and utilizes them to train a deep network-based pose estimator. To further improve performance, the proposed method incorporates 3D surfel-based map reconstruction to optimise the pose estimation. Experiments conducted on the HPM dataset demonstrate that the proposed method positions itself in the middle in terms of accuracy compared to existing two-level relocalisation approaches, and it surpasses them all when dealing with textureless and highly mirrored environments, as evidenced by qualitative results.

In an uplink multi-antenna system utilizing a non-orthogonal protocol, we develop a method utilizing vector modulation to jointly optimize user selection and vector ring coding for joint transmission. Our approach formulates the joint optimization problem as a l1-regularized least squares issue and proposes an iterative algorithm to solve it, leveraging the expansion of the logarithm of the pairwise error probability into its Taylor series. Our numerical results show that our solution yields better performance in terms of bit error rate and transmission spectrum efficiency, and its computation time is comparable to the original formulation.

We introduce a novel creation method for finite semifields utilizing tropical polynomials over a tropical field, as well as tropical curves. This method is analogous to finite fields created through quotient rings of multivariate polynomials, or tropical semifields constructed of free tropical monoids. To demonstrate the efficiency of our approach, we establish that the tropical curve's semifield of its associated automaton has a finite generation property over the corresponding tropical field. Furthermore, finite fields can be produced by isomorphically embedding a tropical curve's semifield into a multivariate tropical polynomial ring, or equivalently, its automaton-based semifield. Our method, being novel and based on tropical geometry, offers a straightforward and effective approach to creating these algebraic structures.

This paper examines how the Q-procedure, a key element of Tarski's game tree framework for modeling sequential games with incomplete information, can be derived from a more fundamental concept called the I-rationalization procedure. By utilizing Fudenberg's convergence argument, the study shows that the F-equilibrium outcomes generated by I-rationalization closely align with those generated by Q-rationalization when players have deeply nested understanding of others' limitations in their information trees. Additionally, the research expands its initial findings by incorporating concepts from Harsanyi's "Thinking, Conditions and Artificial Utility" and Q-equilibrium to Artzner's more comprehensive rationalization framework, which covers concepts like Stochastic Utility Theory and Level-k reasoning.

We have defined a link $L$, a specific 6-component link that can be converted into the Hopf link by changing only two strands, and it is known as the Yuasa-Fox-Hatcher link, a generalization of a simpler three-component link. We have created a novel non-zero Vassiliev invariant that characterizes Fox-Hatcher links of any distinct component number and been able to prove its independence across all component numbers by utilizing a comprehensive table of combinatorial shadow links.

This study presents a modification of the Two Higgs Doublet Model type-III parameterization, incorporating accounting for all relevant experimental data simultaneously. Specific data includes the Higgs mass and properties confirmed by ATLAS and CMS, alongside other data such as Z_h → hh, neutral Higgs masses generated by 13 TeV and 1 TeV ICARCUS simulations, and the proposed Z_h → f \bar{f} decay at 32 TeV and 10 TeV on a muon collider, along with Z_h → \gamma\gamma and Z_h → e \bar{e} decays. Assuming an integrated luminosity of 15 ab^(-1) for the LHC and 5 ab^(- 1) on a 32 TeV muon collider, our code enables exploration of both 125 GeV and additional Higgs boson scenarios, as well as a 3 TeV muon collider with 5 ab^(- 1) luminosity for a single Higgs boson mass of 125 GeV.

By leveraging evolutionary algorithms, our research has successfully established effective methods for guiding the assembly of molecular structures through the design of particle behaviors and manipulation procedures. These search strategies, comprising multiple levels, involve discovering self-replicating particles that utilize available tools and exploring different levels of complexity, including structural and functional hierarchies. These multi-level evolutionary search strategies allow for efficient optimization and lead to successful design of desired molecular structures.

We investigate the anomaly matching conditions in the context of a chiral gauge theory with U(1) symmetry, focusing on its behavior in the low-energy regimes where it either produces a gapless Wess-Zumino-Witten model or transitions into a gapless gapless phase. We explore the possibility that low-energy modes might emerge in the gapless phase, including the condition when the low-energy modes are a specific type of Quantum Critical Spin Liquid with spin U(1) dynamics.

This study examines the solvability of the three-dimensional steady Navier-Stokes equations in periodic domains in relation to initial conditions. We demonstrate in homogeneous Besov spaces that a critical threshold exists below which initial data may yield solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations, a finding that expands upon a previously established result in inhomogeneous Besov spaces, while our result further shows scale invariance in the defining threshold.

In the study of magnons and their collective spin waves of antiferromagnets, a phenomenon of thermal shift was found to occur, initially attributed to magnon-magnon interactions causing frequency changes with temperature increases. Researchers discovered these effects to be manifestations of broader classes of thermal nonlinear phenomena that result in magnon spectrum displacement with temperature. A study was conducted on ferroelectric PbTiO$_3$, in which the behavior of magnons was investigated at room temperature with high spatial resolution. The findings confirmed that magnon spectrum displacement is predominantly due to thermal effects. A notable outcome of these results was that magnon nonlinearity influences both the real and imaginary components of magnon self-energy, necessitating a reassessment of concepts such as nonlocal magnon self-energy. The concept of periodic windows for magnon band structures due to spin waves periodicity was also explored.

This paper explores modifications to Loidreau's code-based cryptography, which is based on a quadratic form code constructed from a random linear code with excellent distance properties, initially proposed to create a quadratic code for cryptosystems. Our findings reveal that in this quadratic form code, the dual's minimum distance is typically very low, making the secret generator matrix of the quadratic form code vulnerable and easily decipherable through various attacks. Moreover, we observe that if the base linear code has double the minimum distance compared to its random counterpart, the resulting quadratic form code is more susceptible to a specific attack. These observations suggest a revision of the Loidreau's quadratic map to enhance the security of the Loidreau's cryptography system.

Machine comprehension tasks like QA and MRTE have seen improvements through the use of large-scale language models pre-trained with masked language modeling. However, their performance is limited by dataset-specific noise and valid word combinations not seen during the pre-training phase. A more robust solution lies in expanding the vocabulary used for training these models. One effective strategy is adding a dictionary of common word pairs to the training data. This study explores adding glossaries to BERT's pre-training process to enhance its ability to capture meaningful word pair connections. Our results demonstrate that adding glossaries to pre-training yields consistent performance gains on the SNLI, MNLI, and QNLI datasets, outperforming existing state-of-the-art models and validating the importance of common word pairs in natural language.

Employing tools from geometric probability and stochastic geometry, we investigate the total volume enclosed by a specific type of network formed from a set of points scattered randomly within a given space. Total volume and limiting shapes of such networks provide valuable insights into their overall structure and complexity. Our research builds upon a recent study that analyzed a related network structure, now extending these findings to more intricate networks with specific properties. Using advanced mathematical concepts, including measure convergence, we establish that these networks develop specific shapes in the long run and determine the total volume and network density within a given space. Our analysis reveals that the networks' limiting shapes resemble a smooth surface with a set of embedded loops that do not intersect, or a collection of such surfaces separated by unique loop patterns. These results deepen our understanding of the networks' internal structure and contribute to broader questions in mathematical research regarding optimal geometric shapes in various spaces.

This study explores the challenges of protecting sensitive student data in Federal Learning when applications utilize aggregation, privacy-preserving techniques, and secure computing. The proposed research examines the efficacy of these existing safeguards by attempting to breach the security of the protocol with specific adversarial actions. The results indicate that, within the context of Federal Learning, the aggregated nature of the released data can be significantly reconstructed from a limited number of queries using simple methods such as Monte-Carlo simulations, posing a significant risk of data leakage for Federal Learning, and suggesting a need for additional protective measures. Furthermore, this paper demonstrates that the federated approach offers substantially lower data leakage compared to traditional centralized training methods without a substantial loss in predictive performance. The research includes a supplementary video resource showcasing the data aggregation attack in Federal Learning.

In a new dark matter model featuring a chiral U(1)_d symmetry, where the dark sector includes dark mesons and baryons, we investigate B meson decays resulting in a dark baryon-antibaryon pair. To calculate relevant matrix elements involving dark mesons, baryons, and B mesons, we utilize the light-cone sum principles method. Notably, we present the structure functions specifically related to the dark baryon. Building on the derived structure functions and the weak Hamiltonian for specific B decay processes, we establish decay rate and branching ratio formulas for B decays into a dark meson-baryon-antibaryon trio. Furthermore, existing experimental constraints from Belle, BaBar, and LHCb, along with an estimation of dark meson-baryon production at a high-energy electron collider, are discussed in relation to the Higgs portal dark matter model.

In a rapidly evolving social and technological landscape, cities face increasing vulnerability to socio-cyber-physical attacks. To defend against such threats, effective management of limited defense resources becomes a critical challenge for urban administrators. We present an innovative defense framework, consisting of a simulation-based attack model and a novel resource allocation algorithm, which enables a comprehensive understanding of attack dynamics and optimal resource distribution strategies within the context of modern urban security. The proposed algorithm outperforms existing benchmarks, effectively minimizing vulnerability in the face of sophisticated cyber and physical assaults.

Researchers have studied how black holes outside and inside a bounding surface change temperature, exhibiting different transitions, which are similar for black holes outside the surface and yield novel results for black holes inside a finite space.

In the context of a multi-label classification task, where each data item can be assigned multiple categories, data retrieval is the process of obtaining the most relevant original classes for each item. This is a complex problem, particularly when dealing with imperfect labels, where traditional approaches are hindered by the label noise-induced ambiguity of the problem. A proposed solution, known as MNRA-beg, addresses this challenge by combining two techniques - the bag sampling method and the group-based Bregman loss - to achieve better label noise-resistant performance and enhanced generalization capabilities. This method outperforms existing approaches, particularly in noisy label environments, and its effectiveness has been thoroughly validated through comprehensive experiments.

The performance of graph neural networks (GNNs) for node classification can be further enhanced by incorporating pseudo-labels. However, generating these labels with semi-supervised learning methods often results in low-quality pseudo-labels. In this paper, a novel approach called FIPT, which stands for Classification and Pseudo-Pseudo-Propagation, is proposed. FIPT leverages the predictions from the GNNs to re-weight the loss function and thereby learn more effectively from both the real and pseudo-labels. FIPT can be integrated with various existing pseudo-relabeling methods and has demonstrated superior performance on different synthetic and real-world datasets, particularly with limited labelled data.

A new experiment at CERN's LHC, called AWAKE, aims to explore the high-density plasma's response to a short, high-energy proton pulse by inducing wakefields and non-linear plasma responses through the Waketron Accelerator concept. A crucial non-linear effect in this concept is the bending motion of trapped electrons, resulting in the production of X-ray photons through the betatron mechanism. A Python-based code, combined with a single plasma diagnostic system, is used to analyze and simulate 100 real plasma shots, and examines the feasibility, mechanisms, and potential sources of noise when detecting betatron emission in AWAKE P1.

This paper introduces a new framework for building secure, privacy-focused distributed decision trees. The framework can be used in any various online settings, including various distributed configurations and online learning scenarios. It features algorithms that are scientifically proven to be trustworthy in protecting customer data. These algorithms can handle multiple data sources, each with their own separate datasets. They are also able to scale up to handle an ever-growing number of customers and features. The study shows how to make these algorithms more secure and accurate by using differential privacy techniques. A secure data transmission layer and accurate tree models are added through multiple decoupled processes and carefully designed constraints. Experiment results using various real-world datasets confirm that these improved algorithms produce performant models with high accuracy and security guarantees.

Achieving effective and interpretable data compression, crucial in machine learning, data science, and related fields, is a pressing need. For a given source of random variables and an allowed error margin, the optimal solution to this problem is a statistical method known as a R\'enyi distance minimization. Unfortunately, closed-form solutions are only feasible for specific scenarios, while for complex situations, an approximation-based approach based on iterative minimization is necessary. The proposed approach presents a new algorithm to solve a broader class of R\'enyen distance minimization problems for discrete random variables, which can be solved efficiently and is guaranteed to find a solution. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated in simulations and practical experiments and is shown to outperform the standard techniques.

A statistical model called chain event graphs, and an advanced version called chain event graphs, have been developed to analyze complex networks, especially those with multiple dependencies. Originally proposed by Dahm and Agresti in 2015, these models allow for flexibility in accommodating various types of event data. An extension of this model, called chain event graphs, was introduced by Dahm and Agresti to simplify the analysis of networks with multiple dependencies. Despite the benefits of visualizing data and analyzing complex networks, the risk of selecting an overly complex model is a concern. To address this issue, we have developed a new method for selecting the most suitable model for a given dataset using Bayesian statistics. This approach, based on maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation, allows for the selection of models that are unlikely to occur by design, thereby reducing the risk of overfitting. We have applied maximum a posteriori estimation to select the most suitable model for a network of criminal relationships, and the results are available in the accompanying R package ChainEventGraphCES.

In finite dimensional spaces, the minimal norm solution of a regularized inverse problem can be reached through several methods. This study demonstrates that the continuous dynamics of the inertial Hamiltonian system, equipped with Tikhonov regularization, and the corresponding discretization using Euler method, both converge asymptotically to the minimal norm solution. Notably, the step size in the discretization can be chosen arbitrarily without compromising stability. Furthermore, the dynamics and the discrete approximation exhibit a convex convergence rate towards the solution set.

Rapid assessment of dynamic systems near equilibrium points, where periodic motions coexist, is crucial in various fields. In particular, small changes in system parameters can lead to significant shifts in the domain of attraction of these periodic orbits, drastically altering the system's behavior. In this study, we introduce a new theoretical framework for studying stability domains in periodic systems and use it to study the stability of barrier-adhering mobile robots. We find that, as a function of the system's friction coefficient, the size of the system's stability domain exhibits a pattern of regular and irregular fluctuations. Notably, we identify regular and irregular intervals within this system and identify a complex, fractal-like structure that separates distinct dynamical behaviors. We validate these findings through numerical simulations and experiments, which reveal that our approach can provide valuable insights into the dynamic behavior of adhesive mobile robots.

In the realm of high-temperature superconductivity, microwaves serve as sensitive probes, but their effectiveness is heavily influenced by impurities and carrier density. By simulating the dynamics of kinetic superfluids with scattered impurities, this study explores how extended impurities in copper-oxide superconductors affect microwave response. Utilizing energy-based superconductivity, it's demonstrated that impurity shape and density, as well as carrier density and energy, all play significant roles in determining microwave response, particularly when the sample is near its critical temperature. Moreover, the study also finds that impurity size shape matters, with sharp features in the impurity potential causing significant response changes at certain frequencies.

This passage discusses a non-smooth, length-preserving method used to analyze convex shapes. In the past, curvature-based approaches were employed to solve problems related to shrinking and expanding bodies consistently. However, the described method utilizes crystalline or anisotropic average curvature instead, effectively bypassing the need for boundary smoothness. These calculations can be carried out using tools from mathematical physics such as proximal maps, total variation models, and variational processes. Convex shapes evolving under this method exhibit total variation convergence, while also demonstrating piecewise smooth boundaries with angles that gradually diminish. Various aspects of this method, including comparison results, equivalence proofs, and relationships between different approaches, along with extensions to problems involving multiple phases and non-convex configurations, are explored.

Plant research has a long history of exploring the intricate relationship between plants and their environment, particularly when it comes to growing conditions. Plants have the ability to grow in various ways in response to external stimuli, and research has recently started to incorporate robotic automation to accelerate the process of discovering optimal growing conditions. To bridge the gap between robotics and plant care, this paper proposes GrowSpace, a framework for investigating and understanding the art of shaping plants through spatial manipulation. By examining case studies on trained hanging plants, GrowSpace sheds light on the principles behind plant shaping and highlights the complexities involved in robotics and plant science collaboration. Through GrowSpace, robotics and plant science can work together to explore new territories in plant care and robot learning.

Dermot Sheffer discovered a connection between the quantum parameter $\beta$ and the SLE parameter $\kappa$, specifically $\beta^2 = \kappa + 2$. Conversely, David Berman found a converse relationship, $\beta^2 = 8 - \kappa$, indicating an intersection of their findings between the ranges $0 \le \kappa \le 4$ and $-2 \le \kappa \le 4$. Building upon Berman's work, we establish that Sheffer's result holds for the specific case of point-to-point SLE with $\kappa \le 4$ and chordal SLE $\kappa \le 4$. Building on Berman's work, we establish that Sheffer's result holds for the specific case of point-to-point SLE with $\kappa \le 4$ and chordal SLE $\kappa \le 4$. Utilizing Berman's findings, we demonstrate that the process of gluing two quantum disks conformally results in a new conformal structure equivalent to gluing them together via SLE $\kappa < 4$. Furthermore, we examine the duals of these processes, demonstrating a connection to the SLE regime with $\kappa \ge 4$, specifically the complement SLE $\kappa < 4 and the SLE $\kappa \ge 4 loop with interior reflections.

The Image Indicator Standardization Initiative (IIS) seeks to standardize key visual metrics used in climate research. As researchers in the field of climate science analyze increasing amounts of visual data, these images serve as a critical tool for scientists to examine and interpret complex climate systems. These images are also essential in communicating complex climate information to a broader audience, including policy makers and the general public. By standardizing image-based climate metrics, the ClIS aims to address current challenges in climate research, such as image comparability, reproducibility, and compatibility.

We have made precise calculations of how the $K\Lambda$ and $K\Sigma$ mesons are produced when a nucleon is hit by a photon, focusing on the high-spin nucleon and delta resonances. The calculations are based on the effective Lagrangian approach and take into account the photoproduction process at the Lagrangian level. Our calculations are consistent with the measured total cross-sections in the high-energy region and closely match the total cross-sections in the $K\Lambda$ photoproduction at lower energies ($K_{Lab} \leq 1.5$ GeV). However, there is a slight underestimation of these results in the low-energy region ($K_{Lab} \leq 1.0$ GeV).

One critical phase in biometric systems is image preprocessing to eliminate
background distractions and enhance subject image quality. Poorly designed
biometric systems are often a result of inadequate image preprocessing, which
can be resolved by implementing robust preprocessing techniques. This research
investigates motion-compensated frequency-domain analysis methods, leveraging
Flitter & Frick's approach, to develop an efficient biometric system. The study
evaluates size reduction techniques leveraging statistical analysis and explores
various edge extraction methods available within the OpenCV framework, including
Laplace, Sobel, and Prewitt transformations. Downscaling methods utilizing steganography and compression methods including JPEG, JPEG2000, and Vector Quantization are also examined in an attempt to reduce the data size without compromising recognition rates. These approaches were tested on over 13500 diverse facial images from the MORPH-II face database to determine the most effective techniques for edge extraction and data size reduction methods.

From the ancient times of our universe, our planet has been inhabited by mysterious beings - the Black Hole Dwellers. They are not among us, but they can be felt, and their presence is known to those who seek their signs. To understand the role of curvaton in shaping the universe's density perturbations, the Black Hole Dwellers' insights are sought. The analysis reveals that our universe's patterns cannot be fully attributed to inflation alone, but may contain an additional, ancient imprint - the legacy of primordial black holes. However, if inflation-generated dark matter exists, the Black Hole Dwellers' presence may be absent. The examination of cosmic structures and gravitational waves also holds clues about the existence of these beings, but the data so far does not conclusively point to it.

Educational institutions are increasingly adopting educational analytics models to enhance student retention, graduation, and employment rates, as well as informed policy-making. In this context, a statistical approach has been developed to model educational trajectories, focusing on institutional pathways rather than individual pathways. However, existing models lack the ability to capture implicit pathways and their characteristics. This research introduces a new latent variable model, focusing on the emergence of implicit pathways between educational milestones, and uses data from multiple institutions to investigate how pathways change over time. The model's effectiveness has been demonstrated through simulations and real-world applications in higher education.

The simultaneous assessment of vehicle platoon assembly for multiple cars is a complex task, made more difficult by the need for real-time processing. Traditional approaches rely on complex algorithms, but the requirement for continuous communication across the entire chain increases the risk of processing delays and potential system failures. To address this issue, we propose a new, automatic regulation strategy using differential games to improve real-time processing capabilities, allowing each vehicle to independently assess the system, and minimizing inter-vehicle communication. This approach also offers energy savings by reducing the frequency of unnecessary communications. A comprehensive analysis of our method's performance has been conducted through simulation tests, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to existing solutions.

The relationship between an explanatory variable and the logistic regression's bias term can be critical, making assumptions about independence essential for accurate parameter estimation in the population. However, researchers often lack the necessary information to determine this relationship, leading them to apply broad assumptions. Our analysis reveals the consequences of these "avoid interaction" assumptions and highlights scenarios where they are valid. Interestingly, adopting these assumptions can simplify estimation and allow us to utilize advanced machine learning techniques to accurately estimate the population parameters. Furthermore, our results suggest that in practical applications, particularly with small datasets, disregarding potential interactions can result in misleading parameter estimates and, consequently, poor model performance.

The realm of Natural Language Processing (NLP) is populated by a diverse array of datasets. Text summarization stands out as a prominent application within this field. A recent study by Zhong et al. (2020) demonstrated that neural networks could effectively detect generated summaries to distinguish them from human-written text. Building on this concept, a novel task was introduced - identifying generated headlines with a comparable approach. The HHS dataset, consisting of 50,000 headlines, was proposed to tackle this new challenge. A conventional BERT model, as well as a specialized BERT model with an additional head for classification, were both found to be ineffective at solving this task. However, when fine-tuned with Layer Normalization (LayerNorm) in the [CLS] state vector, significant performance improvements were observed on three headline datasets. Moreover, adding a BERT classification head to each layer resulted in even better results on the HHS dataset, achieving a notable 28.7 points increase in average accuracy compared to the baseline model.

We developed a simplified model of a spin system in a random arrangement and we found it can create a stable, uniform state of aligned spins at very low temperatures at chemical equilibrium. This uniform state has the same properties in all directions, is symmetric and unchanged over time, and has the same composition whether it's arranged in ordered crystals or disordered structures. By exploring how the system transitions between these states, we discovered two distinct pathways: one for fully disordered systems and another for partially ordered systems, each giving rise to different patterns. These pathways allow us to control the properties of the uniform state, and they can also be used to produce useful magnetic structures with controlled characteristics.

The advancements in large-scale radio telescope technology have led to significant computational challenges for polarization calibration, particularly when processing large datasets at $N$ frequencies and $N$ antennas. By leveraging the advantages of fast Fourier transform algorithms, which rely on grid-based input data, researchers have developed calibration methods that minimize computational complexity. Our proposed approach involves processing large datasets and beam-forming using adapted GRILLIN calibration strategies, which can be parallelized and achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}(N\log{N})$. With proposed GPU-based parallelization, GRILLIN calibration is now feasible, enabling predictions of computational costs for upcoming large telescopes, such as SKA Phase 1, which would process over 5 billion frequency channels with 1024 antennas.

A combined approach comprising both generative adversarial and predictive conditional models proves more effective in producing varied optimal investment portfolio allocations. This unique integration demonstrates that diversity in machine learning outcomes can be achieved through multiple techniques, which can subsequently be refined and consolidated. By initially applying conditional adversarial training, we established investment portfolios exhibiting a degree of diversity. Next, we employed autoencoding conditional generative adversarial training to enhance the diversity while reducing errors. Finally, we verified the efficacy of our diversified portfolios using a statistical analysis and empirical testing.

In this study, the gluon polarized transition matrix element $A_{gq}(N)$ is calculated for the variable flavor number scheme up to $O(\alpha_s^3)$. Calculations were performed with parton distributions from MRST2008 and CT10, yielding results that agree with quantum chromodynamics sum rule findings based on the proton mass, using a scale $\mu^2 \sim \mu_q^2$ and $\mu^2 \sim \mu_g^2$.

In radio-quiet gamma-ray sources such as quasars, accurately measuring the luminous active galactic nuclei is essential. Recent research has revealed discrepancies in the luminosity estimates of these sources based on radio-quiet gamma-ray quasar samples and optical surveys. By applying a Bayesian neural network approach, we have developed a tool for classifying gamma-ray luminous active galactic nuclei using only their optical properties. We have analyzed the performance of our model on training and generalization datasets, revealing the potential inaccuracies in the literature's gamma-ray quasar samples. Furthermore, our results suggest that many sources in the literature's quasar samples may actually be star systems or galactic binary systems.

The rapid growth of social media platforms has significantly affected individuals with varying levels of visual, cognitive, and linguistic capabilities. A substantial number of social media posts contain visual content such as images and GIFs that lack descriptive captions, which hinders the understanding of posts by visually impaired users. To address this concern, there has been an increase in the development of automated systems to generate captions for accessible social media content. To improve this area, a dataset of over 100,000 social media images is presented, which can be used to train and evaluate caption generation models to produce accurate caption generations. To address this concern, we propose the SCS dataset, which comprises images sourced from Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter platforms.

This paper considers n graphs, G_1 through n, that have a set of vertices, P, in common. We investigate under what conditions their hypergraph edge sets combine into a tensorable structure. By defining a game based on the graphs' spectra and eigenvalue bounds, we can determine a maximum number of graphs whose edge sets can be combined into a tensor hypergraph. This leads to an upper limit on the sum of products of graph order and multiplicity of certain eigenvalues. Ultimately, we apply this result to give a maximum number of q-regular bipartite graphs that share a common vertex and have a specified eigen-spectrum.

India's upcoming space initiative, INSIST, a 1-meter Indian space telescope, will revolutionize astronomy's Indian chapter by enabling unprecedented deep sky observations. With a 1-meter diameter and advanced adaptive optics, INSIST will successfully observe distant galaxies and the Milky Way's intricate structures. Its capabilities, including high-resolution imaging and spectroscopy, will facilitate detailed studies of exoplanets and stellar populations. Located at a high altitude, the Somnath Observatory in Leh will provide clear views of the universe, while an innovative and cost-effective manufacturing process will ensure top-tier performance. Insisted collaborations with leading international institutes will broaden INSIST's scientific impact, positioning it as a vital asset for astronomers worldwide.

In clinical trials for Alzheimer's, various cognitive assessments are utilized, 
such as the Alzheimer's Disease Clinical Score and the Mini-Mental State Examination.
These tests, which rely on categorical responses, have limitations in accurately 
measuring cognitive decline and distinguishing between different neurodegenerative 
diseases. Some researchers proposed continuous cognitive assessments to overcome this, 
applying the principles of the Alderson-Brown-Spencer Scale. However, analyzing the 
non-linear relationships in these new assessments poses significant analytical 
challenges. This study presents methods to incorporate the continuous cognitive 
scores into the analysis of related clinical trials and develops statistical tests 
to detect non-linear effects. It utilizes real data to demonstrate the accuracy 
and reliability of these methods in making sound medical decisions.

We introduce a novel approach to investigate rare events under strong noise conditions. Building upon the Wang-Xu solution for stochastic dynamics, our framework identifies transitions following a trajectory that maximizes the difference between the action values in the final and initial states. This method effectively highlights system state changes by emphasizing the dominant transition pathways. As a result, proposed pathways are characterized by a steep decline in action values. To demonstrate the efficacy of this technique, we apply it to numerous examples and compare the outcomes with those from standard sampling techniques in studying rare events in single-barrier and double-well systems. Additionally, we apply the proposed method to a triple-well system with arbitrary barriers, revealing transition pathways under high noise conditions that are unattainable via typical simulation methods. This research offers a practical guide for analyzing rare events in complex systems by providing insight into transition pathways in diverse energy landscapes.

The parabolic versions of complex Monge-Ampere and Hessian equations are offered in L^∞ approximation forms, along with proofs of their uniqueness and stability of solutions in the class of equivalent bounded solutions.

We've developed a 'typed context lambda-calculus with a stronger equality test, which belongs to the family of lambda lambda b. Its typability aligns with the subclass $B$ of regular functions, specifically long and strictly regular functions, which correspond to bounded, regular expressions without the use of star or nested stacks. When modified to include the type $\bot$, this lambda-calculus characterises the entire set of regular functions. Its structure bears resemblance to that of lambda lambda b, which was established by Regnier and has also been further explored by Assaf and Michaux, particularly its typability's connection to the computable functions. Regnier and Machata's work on typed lambda-calculi characterising the class of regular functions found in $A$ has also influenced our related work, which aims to characterise another subclass of regular functions using a similar lambda-calculus.

In this study, we consider a generalized Stratonovich and Ito interpretation of the one-dimensional integral for a function that depends on a stochastic process satisfying certain properties such as Markovness and conditional distribution requirements. We establish a relationship between the corresponding Stratonovich and Ito integrals in terms of the latter's drift term, which can be expressed using a conditional probability measure based on a given property of the stochastic process. Our findings also reveal the representation of the stochastic derivative in terms of a generalized conditional Drift function, and this can be expressed using a measure of a corresponding conditional score function. This result is extended to the case of the multi-dimensional integral for a function that depends on a conditional distribution flow for a stochastic process across multiple dimensions by means of a representation of the generalized conditional Drift in terms of a linear combination of a set of basis functions, and a representation of the generalized conditional score function across the state space. In the two-dimensional case, we also show the connection between a multi-dimensional integral for a function that depends on a stochastic process and a corresponding Stratonovich Ito integral in terms of a backward stochastic differential equation for a function that minimizes a cost function. We apply our results to the case of the stochastic differential equation for a process that has certain properties such as a coefficient that satisfies certain assumptions, and show the representation of a corresponding Stratonovich Ito integral in terms of a stochastic derivative of a function that satisfies certain properties.

A discrete structure, known as a discrete space, is referred to as an N-space in literature. Researchers in various fields such as topology, semigroup theory, and geometry study compact Hausdorff groups with discrete subgroups and symmetry groups. They examine these objects using separation axioms and maximal groups. Specific examples include the maximal torus and the space of discrete subgroups. Notably, the space of discrete subgroups is Hausdorff if and only if it matches with a certain group structure. It's also found that this space of discrete subgroups is topologically distinct from another space of group elements. Consequently, it follows that if a compact Hausdorff group has more than two elements, its space of discrete subgroups cannot be homeomorphically mapped to an N-space.

Current text-to-SQL models excel at extracting individual SQL components from user queries but often fail to ensure overall query coherence and understand the complete context of the dataset SQL. Notably, existing approaches don't facilitate a unified understanding of both data SQL and user queries in a unified parsing framework, resulting in a poor performance on cross-domain tasks. To address these challenges, we introduce CrossDom, a novel end-to-end framework that effectively performs cross-domain text-to-SQL parsing. It leverages a supportive task to ensure meaningful text-to-SQL parsing and incorporate a global SQL comprehension. The results show that our method achieves superior performance, boasting an F1-score of 85.02% on the Spider dataset and cross-domain scores of 84.0% on the source domain and 78.8% on the target domain, surpassing the state-of-the-art results by a margin of 1.9%.

This work introduces a time-efficient, robust time-clipped Stochastic Risk-averse Model Predictive Control (TRC-SRMPC) approach for multi-robot management. To reduce computational costs, each robot's movement is restricted within a limited time frame. To minimize movement conflicts, a novel local time-clipped Stochastic Risk-averse Model Predictive Control (TRC-SRMPC) strategy is proposed, enabling short-term movement predictions based on current time-clipped trajectories. Extensive simulations demonstrate that the integrated TRC-SRMPC method offers lower computational latency and lower movement conflicts compared to current robust and risk-averse MPC techniques. Notably, when compared to heuristic risk-averse strategies, the simulated results show a significant reduction in trajectories of more than 8%, along with lower computational latency.

Researchers have made a new discovery called Andromeda XXV, a small satellite galaxy orbiting Andromeda, located about 200 kpc away with an apparent magnitude of 18.5. Based on its high velocity and small dispersion, its mass is estimated to be between 5 billion and 10 billion solar masses. Notably, Andromeda XXV has a high metal content, exceeding 0.1, a high S/N ratio, a high SFR, a low dark matter to baryon ratio in its core, and a low dark matter density in its core compared to other galaxies of its size. These characteristics suggest that Andomeda XXV has undergone significant tidal disruption.

In mass connectivity systems, users transmit data simultaneously to the base station without receiving allocation, resulting in the need for the base station to separate user signals using specific patterns or sequences. Current studies primarily concentrate on orthogonal patterns, which are limited in application to a small number of users. To overcome this limitation, we propose a method for designing patterns applicable to a large number of users and channels, where signals are transmitted using a direct sequence spread spectrum technique, which is resilient to channel variations. We utilize a two-stage genetic algorithm to generate non-orthogonal patterns, significantly reducing the search space and providing a suitable fitness function for pattern design, which is evaluated through simulations to demonstrate improved system performance, especially at low and medium signal-to-noise ratios.

A numerical multi-phase flow model for mist dynamics has been developed and developed to account for drop movements and interactions within atmospheric conditions. This model utilizes continuum mechanics to simulate the transport equations governing mist dynamics, considering the thermodynamic state of humid air through the introduction of appropriate source terms. These equations were designed in accordance with the first and second laws of thermodynamics, using thermodynamically accurate formulas based on the theory of maximum entropy. Approximations were made to the theory of maximum entropy formulas to derive the source terms, and four types of approximations were identified and analyzed for their accuracy and reliability. Each approximation was tested for its ability to maintain thermodynamic consistency and correctly predict mist dynamics, with notable discrepancies found for one of the approximations, leading to potential issues with energy conservation and entropy production principles.

We introduce a concept of outer algebra within the framework of matroid theory, and demonstrate its connections to various areas of mathematics, including fixed fields of linear groups, fixed groups of linear groups, and fixed algebras of noncommutative algebras. To solidify this concept, we establish the outer algebra theorem for matroids, which provides a comprehensive foundation for outer algebras.

In tasks such as dialogue management and response selection, accurately tagging user intents and extracting relevant information are critical tasks that rely on the relative probability scores of top intent and entities candidates. These scores can be effectively guided by a model that predicts the uncertainty of transcribed utterances, trained using a dataset constructed from word confusion networks.

For any curve, we can define a sequence of functions that give the maximum estimated number of stable sheaves with specific dimensions and fixed degrees. In the case of generic curves of a higher genus, exact functions are known, whereas for curves of genus two, specific calculations can be done. Furthermore, we prove a genericity result for polarized curves and utilize it to compute functions on curves of genus two. Lastly, we calculate the upper bound on the number of rank two stable sheaves on curves of genus two.

A key feature of complex theories is the presence of multiple essential components that work together in a coherent framework. Researchers in computer science have developed various frameworks for web and program analysis, and these frameworks can be categorized as either high-level abstract models or low-level concrete models. We observe two main patterns in organizing these frameworks: a hierarchical bottom-up approach and a top-down approach. We found that a more intuitive bottom-up framework often ends up being more complex and difficult to implement, whereas the simpler-looking top-down framework can actually hide underlying complexity and prove to be more efficient in practical terms and ease of use. Furthermore, the theoretical analysis indicates that the difference in practicality and usability between competing frameworks can be quite significant and even theoretically non-negligible depending on the size of the problem at hand, thereby demonstrating that theory can sometimes show substantial practical differences.

We introduce an optimized method for quantifying entanglement in complex optical states, which contain an arbitrary superposition of different numbers of photons. Our technique leverages measurements from shift-based homodyne systems, offering a more efficient alternative to traditional parity checks on individual photons. It surpasses existing parity-based methods in clarity and efficiency. Our method challenges pre-set assumptions about optimal measurement techniques for analyzing quantum entanglement. Furthermore, our results can be adapted to other multi-photon quantum states, enabling the efficient verification of quantum circuits. This technique holds significant value in resolving ongoing debates about optimal measurement outcomes in optical quantum computing systems.

The complex process of forming non-linear plasma instabilities is difficult to model accurately. Research on this topic at a computer center in Italy has yielded valuable insights into Palm Tree Modes in the JET tokamak. These modes, characterized by specific spatial patterns, are thought to be essentially driven by eddy currents. A new approach to studying these modes has been developed, which involves breaking down their movement and shape using a set of universal mathematical concepts. By applying this approach to various simulated scenarios, scientists have been able to identify the key underlying mechanisms that give rise to these modes. The investigation revealed two distinct modes, one linear and high-frequency, and the other non-linear and relatively slow-moving. These findings confirm that EDN is the primary driver of Palm Tree Modes, while also suggesting that their higher-order features may be influenced by additional physical factors. The study provides new understanding of these modes, which is valuable for modeling their behavior in plasmas.

Pretrained models, which are trained on large, extensive datasets, have revolutionized computer vision. Their generic nature allows them to be applied to tasks other than the one originally trained for, utilizing transfer learning techniques to fine-tune the model. This approach typically yields positive results. However, an important question remains: can these models' powerful ability to transfer knowledge be combined with online learning methods to continuously adapt to new environments and perform the same task over multiple iterations? Our study investigates several online learning algorithms, including replay-based methods, using pretrained models, and discovers that these methods often fail to learn sequentially, even when provided with ample experience, when the involved tasks are based on visual similarities. Our research reveals that recurrent recurrent experience is a key factor in enabling recurrent learning, and that recurrent models can surpass recurrent algorithms, especially when combined with a well-organized and chronologically ordered curriculum of learning tasks that leverages the underlying data's chronological structure.

The surge in the use of social media has made it increasingly common to spread hate speech, which poses a significant threat to global peace. Automatically detecting and mitigating hate speech on social media has become a pressing concern for researchers around the world. To improve upon existing and proposed approaches, this study focuses on multi-modal inputs and the incorporation of visual modality. A new framework called UMNet is introduced, combining deep learning with rule-based methods, to identify and classify hate speech across multiple categories from both image and text inputs. By integrating a knowledge graph-driven rule-based system, UMNet demonstrates notable performance gains, especially in identifying subtle categories of hate speech. UmNet is further used to analyze the characteristics of multi-modal hate speech and the associated topics, providing insights into the phenomenon. UmNet, along with detailed user instructions, is made publicly available at [https://github.com/abhi1989/UMNet](https://github.com/abhi1989/UMNet).

Neural networks formed from type-I neurons play a key role in understanding how neurons communicate and how neural systems produce rhythmic patterns and other dynamic behaviors. Research has shown that the random geometric graph model can accurately simulate certain features of these neural systems and that the formation of同步 rhythms in these models is a result of a particular bifurcation pattern that can be influenced by the distribution of neuron positions. A recent study aimed to determine the effects of extending the range of neuron positions on the model parameters that affect synchronization, and it was found that while position distributions affect some parameters, they do not influence others. A notable outcome was that extending the range of neuron positions did not lead to a change in the type of bifurcation that influences synchronization, indicating that type-I neurons can still achieve synchronized states through a pitchfork bifurcation even when the range of neuron positions is greatly expanded.

Program reverse engineering has been long utilized in software reverse engineering. Recently, deep learning approaches have gained significant attention. Our investigation reveals that determining the precise location of debugging fixes is a critical issue in automated debugging. Our proposed Antagonistic Patch Creation (APC) technique leverages the principle of program equivalence to generate multiple versions of the buggy program, thereby facilitating the identification of the correct debugging fix through the analysis of the inverse dependencies among the patches. We implemented an algorithm based on APC and evaluated it with the most widely-used benchmark, DefForma. The experimental results demonstrate that the technique effectively enhances the initial buggy input and improves the overall performance of the proposed method.

A comprehensive capability boundary is constructed for the generalized information flow callback (GIFC) problem. It is demonstrated that the GIFC problem can be approximated within a factor of one using this capability region. The capability region is defined by integrating the capability boundaries of the noninteractive setting. An important computational method known as the data spectrum is utilized to calculate a segment of the capability boundary corresponding to the specific information flow callback problem. To address data spectrum's primary algorithmic limitation, which restricts the flow of information, a novel data spectrum definition is proposed, referred to as the information flow data spectrum. It is shown that for the GIFC problem, the data spectrum approach yields an accurate representation by calculating an approximate minimum of the information transmission rate in an independent channel configuration where information is shared among all users. It is demonstrated that the information transmission rate is an unbroken function. To resolve the problem of non-differentiability, a specific algorithm called the subgradient method is employed to compute a precise approximation. It is proven that this approximate minimum provides a reliable solution with an accurate accuracy factor. To validate the method, an independent channel configuration where information is shared among all users is applied to a practical case study analyzing the security of the Wireshark tool.

The nuclear equation-of-state (EOS) in the context of symmetric, cold nuclear matter is primarily defined by its two key parameters: the speed of sound ($c_s$) and the incompressibility ($K_0$). The relationship between the speed of sound and the mass-energy ratio ($M/\rho$) provides valuable insights into the behavior of nuclear matter under extreme conditions, ultimately influencing flow patterns and observables in heavy-ion collisions. The interplay between EOS parameters and observables, such as $v_3$ and $R_{flow}$, is crucial in understanding the dynamics of ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions and the properties of quark-gluon plasma.

Recent advancements in deep learning have led to a significant surge in research exploring deep neural networks in various applications, including medical image analysis. Researchers are increasingly focused on using deep learning models to analyze chest X-ray and CT scans for detecting COVID-19, yet the majority of studies rely on raw data without accounting for potential adversarial attacks or a significant proportion of private patient information. This research aims to address these shortcomings by developing an early diagnosis system for COVID-19 that integrates adversarial training and weight pruning techniques. Our method is designed to enhance the network's resilience against adversarial attacks and reduce data storage needs and inference time. Our analysis reveals that incorporating adversarial training not only yields superior classification accuracy but also contributes to better privacy protection. Furthermore, we conducted a thorough evaluation of our proposed approach on external datasets, demonstrating that it promotes generalization. Our results indicate that the adversarial training method we employed can offer robust privacy protection for the lung abnormality detection model, with promising potential for adoption in medical image analysis.

The integration of wireless sensing with communication systems is expected to significantly enhance the performance of these systems by providing additional information, a concept known as sensing-aware wireless communication (WSAC). A proposed framework, Decentralized Graph Neural Networks, integrates wireless sensing and communication capabilities within a single end-to-end system architecture. This innovative approach, centered around a wireless communication hub, utilizes a sensing node to gather and relay measurement data to enhance wireless communication, thereby optimizing transmission efficiency through minimal feedback interactions.

A comprehensive examination of the public security secretary's data from the Brazilian state of Goias, spanning 2002 to 2014, has led to a computer program's development. This program calculates spatial statistics for continuous fields, specifically the Global Moran's I, and identifies anomalous areas through statistical tests. Its output cautions administrators against relying on statistical significance as the primary indicator for intervention, as highlighted in the study. Additionally, the investigation revealed areas with elevated homicide rates, which necessitate targeted government and law enforcement action.

Our study conducts a mathematical analysis of stochastic gradient ascent as applied to maximization problems. In contrast to typical results for stochastic gradient descent, which indicate convergence under certain conditions, it is found that stochastic gradient ascent can lead to significant solution drift due to natural noise. In this study, an enhanced version of stochastic gradient ascent is developed, which can naturally resist the adverse effects of noise. This enhanced ascent is shown to converge to an optimal solution under a specific low learning rate and a high challenge ratio, which reflects how well the loss landscape can be navigated. Furthermore, numerical experiments verify that this enhanced gradient ascent can be conditionally accelerated while still achieving optimal performance. In addition, it is found that increasing the challenge ratio can significantly reduce solution drift even with decreasing challenge adaptability. As a consequence, it is possible to achieve a balance between acceleration and convergence in dynamic optimization problems.

A widely accepted concept holds that the Sun's core is the only place where
nuclear fusion takes place, yet it remains challenging to study this area due to
its extreme conditions. To this end, we propose utilizing axion search results
from the BabyIAXO experiment, which aims to validate the axion hypothesis and
determine the axion-gluon coupling constant. Our research demonstrates that
babyIAXO's sensitivity to axions can confirm their presence within the Sun's
core with high confidence. Furthermore, we outlines two methods for
cross-verifying this confirmation: (a) analyzing time-varying axion signals as
the Earth orbits the Sun and noting the signal's onset around late August, prior
to the full-year maximum observed in the second experiment; or (b) detecting an
axion signal that remains consistently present even when the sun is at the center
of the sky in June. Additionally, we discuss additional advantages of observing
the Sun at its closest point.

We propose a novel class of deterministic self-exciting systems and explore their key characteristics. Specifically, we introduce an external mechanism that drives a periodic change in system dynamics, leading to auto oscillations. By applying concepts from Morse theory, we derive conditions for existence of auto oscillations in systems with one, two, or three equilibria. To illustrate our findings, we analyze a three-dimensional reaction-diffusion model representing excitability in biological cells.

Robot manipulation requires grasp planning, and developing effective grasp policies is crucial for robotic manipulation. Recent advancements in deep learning-based methods, however, require substantial labeled depth images for supervised training, a task made difficult due to the lack of available data. To address this issue, proposed in this paper is an efficient data labeling approach that leverages a universal joint to acquire multi-fingered grasp data that can be applied to a wide range of objects. Moreover, a large-scale dataset, known as DexGraspNet, is presented, which facilitates research into representation learning for robotic manipulation.

We have developed a novel free-breathing four-dimensional T2-weighted turbo spin-echo MRI technique, which enables high-resolution three-dimensional anatomical and respiration-adjusted bodily imaging. This approach leverages the inversion-recovery turbo spin-echo sequence, employing a multi-shot spatial encoding strategy combined with respiration-triggered averaging and the non-Cartier trajectory technique. This innovative technique is specifically designed to acquire high-resolution 3D and 4D (3D+respiration) data during a single breath-hold in approximately 15 minutes, thus enabling the investigation of various organs. This approach was successfully applied to a healthy 27-year-old female volunteer, who provided in-phase and out-of-phase data of her abdomen, thorax, and respiratory movement trajectory, thus allowing for the identification of optimal imaging ranges. This technique was subsequently utilized to acquire a thymus mass from the same volunteer, who had undergone a thymectomy. This research paper presents the results of a non-Cartier, free-breathing multi-echo turbo spin-echo imaging technique, which supports in vivo thymus imaging without the need for surgery. This research supports the availability of the corresponding source code via the following link: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7145353.

This paper introduces InDistill, a new model reduction technique based on knowledge distillation that takes into account data flow during the training process. In contrast to traditional distillation, InDistill leverages a more efficient data flow through in-depth distillation, allowing for the creation of smaller models with enhanced performance. Our experiments demonstrate that InDistill yields reduced models with comparable accuracy to leading model reduction methods, while achieving further accuracy improvements when combined with transfer learning. Notably, InDistill outperforms other approaches in terms of parameter efficiency and accuracy optimization. Our research is accompanied by a GitHub repository providing open-source code and pre-trained networks.

Our analysis demonstrates that a generic smooth projection from the plane to a number line either considerably simplifies into a linear projection or heavily incorporates essential data. This leads to a key observation that such a projection behaves much like a linear one, focusing on the center of the space. Consequently, we conclude that there exists a continuous transformation of the plane to itself such that the projection equals the transformation's projection. Building upon this result, we show that almost all such projections allow for a topological equivalence between the curves created by constant values. Conventional methods for examining submersion projections involve studying curves, spaces, and their mappings more deeply, whereas our research takes a more topological approach.

In desert landscapes, wind-blown water droplets play a crucial role in plant survival. However, plants' ability to access this water relies on wind-driven movements, which can be influenced by an equilibrium between falling droplets and evaporation. As an alternative to point-source rain, non-local foraging refers to the process where water droplets that fall to the ground are redistributed by the wind, thereby increasing the likelihood of droplets settling in other locations. This non-local foraging effect is modeled mathematically and studied to understand its impact on plant dynamics, particularly in plant-vegetation deserts where the coexistence of cacti and grasses is of interest. Through mathematical analysis, it is shown that non-local foraging can alter the stability of steady states, leading to changes in system behavior. These changes include transitions between different types of stability, which can have significant implications for the coexistence of different vegetation types in desert landscapes.

A novel count sketch algorithm, particularly designed to withstand intentional malfeasance, has been developed, focusing on scenarios where an adversary has access to specific input details. This algorithm is the first of its kind in these specific scenarios and can also be effectively applied when input is randomly selected, thus maintaining performance. Performance under randomly selected input is consistent with traditional methods, while for randomly selected adversarial inputs, it even surpasses the efficiency of existing methods that account for adversarial inputs. This improved performance can be attributed to a key property where increasing data size or set count does not count towards the adversary's knowledge, allowing for enhanced robustness. This property also enables the establishment of robustness without compromising for additional data processing requirements.

ie  represents a novel, Python-based software package for auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo methods, designed to enhance both adaptability and efficiency.  ie's primary design goal was to facilitate auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo research in particle and atomic physics, particularly in the study of nuclear systems, by providing an easily accessible and efficient simulation tool that can be used on central processing units or graphical processing units.  ie's innovative development prioritized clear, efficient code written in the Python language, along with an advanced C API optimized for high-performance parallel processing.  ie's auxiliary-field Monte Carlo sampling, which is based on the path integral representation of the Anderson impurity model, has proven to be an effective, flexible, and generally applicable solution for approximating dense electronic structure matrices, particularly those used to describe open-shell systems and correlation-rich atomic structures.  ie's efficiency was further enhanced through advanced parallel processing capabilities enabled by the Advanced Scientific Computing Library (ASL), allowing it to take full advantage of both central and graphical processing units.  ie's features can be easily extended through the use of a straightforward and straightforwardly accessible Python interface that allows users to access and modify low-level operations efficiently.

This research investigates how quantum algorithms could change the outcomes of the classic game known as Prisoner's Dilemma when played in the context of stock trading. utilizing the Draper element as the source of randomization in cooperation between players. Experiments with Draper's quantum processor showed that its generated frequencies can give an advantage to players who use it, even without active interference. Frequencies above 20 MHz resulted in consistently higher rates of mutual cooperation between players. These findings support the use of Draper as a reliable tool for cooperative strategies in quantum computing.
I'm developing a framework for residents to make informed decisions about using intermediaries in exchange for reduced prices, effective for any range of pricing strategies.

To create a plausible reconstruction of past events summarized in someone's mind, we must first develop a planning model that incorporates the constraints and significance of those events. In our approach, we treat planning as a classification problem where we classify actions based on the events summarized. A key innovation in our approach is the use of prompt-based learning which enables us to utilize a large language model effectively without the need for a complex planning layer. Furthermore, our results show that the content of the prompts directly impacts the content of the generated summary, making prompt design a crucial factor in the summarization task. In the context of the PL4DCS dataset, we examine how varying the prompts leads to different, and at times contradictory, interpretations of events. To address this, we have developed a framework called AEPL, which utilizes a meta-learning strategy to adjust the prompts dynamically and generatereconstructions of events that are in line with the summarized events.

This note presents sufficient conditions for a function with $n$ real-valued variables to have a total derivative at a given point, based on the assumption that its partial derivatives with respect to any $n-1$ variables are continuous at that point and have a common sign in a surrounding neighborhood.

Researchers have established a link between speech rate adjustments in individual words within a dialogue and the level of cognitive engagement or cognitive proximity between people. To capture this adjustment, our study focuses on developing a computational method that considers the distinction between rate changes within and across phrases. Using data from interactions of 15 same-sex twin pairs, we evaluated the effectiveness of the proposed computation and found it correlated significantly with observations of cognitive engagement in twinning, compared to other models. This result suggests that the proposed calculation accurately identifies cognitive engagement in natural speech patterns.

Within the framework of unitary sphere theory, researchers seek to elucidate non-unitary phenomena through the reinterpretation of apparent non-unitarity as specialized regulatory mechanisms influenced by environmental factors. As an extension of this theory, researchers have explored the concept of a unitary sphere with a fixed radius and a parameterized direction defined by the lambda angle. The findings demonstrate that this lambda angle exhibits a dual behavior characterized by two complementary regimes: a continuous evolution domain akin to a sphere and a parameterized flat domain resembling a plane. These findings reveal that the lambda angle acts as a quantum regulatory mechanism, with continuous evolution promoting agent stability and parameterization facilitating functional adaptability and the emergence of complex behaviors such as phase transitions and universality classes. The research further establishes a foundational framework for analyzing the stability and adaptability of quantum systems, with implications that the dual regulation of the lambda angle can be applied to various domains such as quantum computing, quantum machine learning, and fundamental studies of general quantum phenomena.

The dynamics of two disturbances in fractional quantum Hall states with Laughlin fillings can be mathematically described by the radial part of the two-particle wave function in the classical limit. The resulting equations are complex and non-linear, and previous studies have yielded approximate solutions. In contrast, this research presents both the full and simplified versions with analytical radial equations for both even and odd scenarios. The key technique involves separating the force and non-force-based two-particle interactions and combining them using specific functions. By making a specific assumption based on this separation, it becomes possible to create a harmonic potential and subsequently derive exact solutions for all cases with various Hall fillings, when expressed in terms of Landau levels.

In the field of numerical modeling of thin ice sheets, a semicoercive variational inequality based on Stokes equations and an adherence constraint is considered, which proves mathematically challenging due to its underlying issues. Consequently, a Kuhn-Tucker multiplier formulation that incorporates the multiplier in both trial and admissible spaces has been developed, thereby facilitating the analysis of a constrained finite element approximation. This approach reveals the presence of different convergence rates for ice flow and multiplier, respectively.

We have analyzed data from the ALMA telescope's Band 3 and the VLT's K-band instruments to create a comprehensive map of the relationship between dust, gas, and newly formed stars in a starbursting spiral galaxy called NGC 5253, which has a high star formation rate. The data reveals that a powerful outflow is originating from the central region of the galaxy and has reached distances of over 10 kiloparsecs. The outflow's velocity increases with distance from the galaxy's center, reaching over 800 kilometers per second. The outflow contains a high amount of fast-moving molecular hydrogen, which has been detected in Band 3 data, which is unusual as this type of data typically does not show such features. The outflow has also been found in the K-band, which is associated with the ultraviolet radiation from the stars. The outflow's total momentum is within the range of other galaxies that have been studied, which suggests that the outflow plays an important role in regulating the star formation in this galaxy.

The triangular flow, denoted as $v_3$, is a crucial early-stage characteristic of heavy-ion collisions, offering insights into the collision's initial conditions, including its temperature and density. A widely-used multiphase transport (AMPHAT) model accurately replicates $v_3$ for Au+Au collisions at a low energy of 20 GeV/nucleon, but fails to capture the expected increase in $v_3$ with decreasing energy for OH-NG, implying a necessary adjustment is required, such as the incorporation of an additional initial energy density. Additionally, AMPHAT demonstrates good agreement with the measured $v_3$ for Cu+Cu collisions at 39 GeV, and the ELASTIC HADRON SCATTERING (ELASTIC HADRON SCATTERING) model of CU+CU collisions at the LHC, and it is observed that the calculation of $v_3$ is insensitive to several model parameters, including the equation of state and charge dependent collisions. Furthermore, ELASTIC HADRON SCATTERING model shows that the variance in $v_3$ measurements can be attributed to differences in initial density, and this may be due to either initial conditions or energy loss during the collision.

This research introduces the concept of SimRobStruc, a pioneering simultaneous robotic structure optimization method. By leveraging robustness, SimRobStruc enables creation of optimal task-specific structures for parallel-series robotic arms that ensure stability and balance. The proposed approach employs an enhanced version of the Extended Castigliano Theorem to define a new Robust Compliance Minimization (RCM) objective, allowing optimization of geometric parameters like length, height, and angle for O-bot platforms using their proprietary optimization tools. A thorough evaluation of RobCast and SimRobStruc on an O-bot platform and an OWL-1 heavy-duty parallel-series robot, demonstrates O-bot's capacity for multi-domain SimRobStruc. Furthermore, O-bot's improved structural robustness and enhanced payload capabilities can be achieved through SimRobStruc, increasing its payload by as much as 50% in certain scenarios.

Deep neural network architecture pre-training has been shown to significantly
impact the performance of deep semantic segmentation. Although there are numerous
pre-training tasks available, the impact of different methods on segmentation
results is not fully understood. In our research, we investigate the performance
of pre-training using various approaches, including image classification, object
retrieval, and depth estimation. We evaluate pre-trained models on the Cityscape
dataset, finding that models trained on a monocular depth assessment task outperform
the others, including the ImageNet dataset. In addition, we examine the impact of
pre-training data quantity, quality, and the choice of base network architecture.
Our analysis reveals that the MONSCC dataset, used for depth assessment, yields
better semi-supervised segmentation results than the larger COCO dataset. Moreover,
we find that using a pre-trained model can significantly reduce the depth estimation
error, even when the pre-training dataset does not include scenes from the test
environment, indicating that the learned depth features are highly transferable.

This research aims to establish the precise value of the Bohr radius within the context of starlike log-harmonic functions, ultimately enhancing the previously proposed radius by Bruna-Sheng. The findings have further far-reaching implications, providing the optimal Bohr radius for the classes $H^{\ast}$ and $G_H$, in addition to several other function classes.

This research introduces methods to reduce calculation complexity when estimating Kendall's tau in large datasets. It enhances the efficiency of the "last element" concept initially proposed by the TETRAD project in Prolog. Building upon this concept, the study provides two new techniques for minimizing computation. The first strategy, known as the "row hash table" approach, initially offered a suboptimal time complexity. A more refined variant, called "last elements in rows," improves time complexity to O(N*M). A second strategy, called "last elements in columns," further contributes to computational efficiency. The study evaluates the strategies under two differing scenarios. When preconditions are met, the combined application of these strategies yields a time complexity of O(N*M) and memory complexity of O(min(N, M)), where N represents the size of the first dimension and M represents the size of the second dimension.
